items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1958-05-31
items.q: And I played one job with Barney D. Gardner. When I worked with King Oliver.

ctx.x: Hold on, I don't hurt, the storm won't hurt that I don't think. Well, that kind of... Instead of picking up all the rain, you hear the rain on here and the, uh, thunder. I guess that won't be the tornado they predicted maybe anyway, we hope not.

So, them kind of fellas, I can tell you a lot about them, because I know them, I work with majority of them. Now we couldn't come to Jimmy Noon. I work with Jimmy Noon. My last recording on the deck was, you remember, with Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon and everybody. Johnny Dotson. My last recording on the deck. Johnny Dotson and Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon's a good musician. Read clarinet parts like nobody's business. I mean clarinet parts. And Johnny Dots could read clarinet parts. Very few clarinet parts you can find read…
Barney is your cousin. My cousin.

items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1967-11-15
items.q: He said, you want to go play the matinee for me, Dreamland? He paid me well, too.

ctx.x: That's a smooth little drum. And Dave would kick his drum just like Benny. Oh, he shoved rhythm and he killed you. Little bit of guy, little Dave Tuff. Gene Krupa, what made Gene Krupa got out of Benny Goodman's band,

and you can, if you see him, son, tell him I'll say, of course, you're going to hit that on the recording, eh? Yes. They had an adjo dance. He couldn't play the first full measure of the introduction. He finished that, huh? He said, well, Gene, I have to get rid of you. You're a dream. Because you've got to win that play. And that's what I liked about your uncle, Johnny. That dad, you're a German, anything they put down on those notes on the paper, he said, all right, bring all the notes off that paper. Bring it…
So, he died. They buried his planet with him. His planet, his planet, his planet,
